newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. appeals for federal prison funding.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. appeals for federal prison funding.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson appealed on Wednesday to U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno to review a decision denying the state's share of federal prison construction funds.
The Office of Justice Programs reached a tentative decision to deny California the so-called "Truth-in-Sentencing" incentive grant funds.

It denied the state the funds because California inmates serving indeterminate life sentences did not meet the federal law's requirement that criminals serve 85 percent of their sentence, Wilson said in a statement.
Of the 145,200 inmates in California prisons, only 10,256 are serving indeterminate life sentences and only 31 have been paroled over the last five years, Wilson said.

"Given this, it seems clear that it would be unfair to deny California access to these critical funds based on a very technical application of the 1994 Crime Act, as amended, and on a dispute over whether or not 31 out of 145,200 inmates in California did not serve 85 percent of their indeterminate life sentences," Wilson wrote in his letter to Reno.
According to the California Department of Corrections, the state's share of the Truth-in-Sentencing grants would be about $255 million over the next five years.
Wilson said the federal funds would be a primary source of revenues for prison construction due to the increase in California's prison population.
He asked Reno to personally oversee a review of the decision.
